svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "One 28-day menstrual cycle: what happens in the ovary, the hormone levels in the blood and the lining of the uterus."], [1.0, "Days 1\u20135, menstruation: progesterone is low, so the endometrium is shed. FSH from the pituitary starts follicles growing."], [4.888888888888889, "Follicular phase: the growing follicle secretes oestradiol, which rebuilds the endometrium."], [9.555555555555555, "High oestradiol triggers the LH surge (positive feedback): a small FSH peak goes with it."], [11.11111111111111, "Day 14, ovulation: the mature follicle bursts and releases the egg."], [12.666666666666668, "Luteal phase: the corpus luteum secretes progesterone, keeping the lining thick and inhibiting FSH and LH (negative feedback)."], [18.88888888888889, "No fertilisation: the corpus luteum degenerates, progesterone and oestradiol fall, the lining breaks down and a new cycle begins."]]
svg.title: The menstrual cycle
svg.desc: A 28-day menstrual cycle aligned on one time axis: follicle development and ovulation in the ovary, FSH and LH from the pituitary, oestradiol and progesterone from the ovary, and the thickness of the endometrium.
svg.text: The menstrual cycle: ovary, hormones and uterus
A typical 28-day cycle. Hormone levels are relative, not to scale with each other.

g.data-info: Each month FSH makes a few follicles grow; one becomes a mature (Graafian) follicle full of fluid with the secondary oocyte inside.
The LH surge makes the mature follicle burst and release the egg (secondary oocyte) into the oviduct.
The empty follicle becomes the corpus luteum (“yellow body”). It secretes progesterone and some oestradiol. Without pregnancy it breaks down after about 10–12 days.
Follicle-stimulating hormone, from the anterior pituitary. Stimulates follicles to grow and secrete oestradiol.
Luteinising hormone, from the anterior pituitary. A sudden surge, triggered by high oestradiol (positive feedback), causes ovulation and forms the corpus luteum.
From the growing follicle. Makes the endometrium thicken again after menstruation; at a high level it triggers the LH surge.
From the corpus luteum. Keeps the endometrium thick and full of blood vessels, ready for implantation, and inhibits FSH and LH (negative feedback).
Shed during menstruation (days 1–5), rebuilt under oestradiol, then maintained by progesterone. When progesterone falls, it breaks down again.

g.text: progesterone inhibits FSH and LH (negative feedback)
